Katowice Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Katowice, Poland

Not demolished. Katowice's cemetery has operated continuously since its official opening in September 1869, with burials dating back to that year and continuing today — one of the few genuinely active, unbroken Jewish cemeteries in this collection. Local Jewish settlement began in the mid-19th century and, though the community was largely deported and killed during WWII, roughly 1,500 Jews resettled in Katowice afterward, mainly deportees returning from the USSR, sustaining an active community to this day. The grounds hold tombstones ranging widely in style and preservation, alongside a mortuary and burial-society building that have fallen into disrepair even as the cemetery itself remains in use and listed on Poland's Immovable Monuments Registry.
